name: bm-r6-perlecan-growth-perturbations
title: Perlecan & growth perturbations on cell shape
claim: CONTRADICTION FLAGGED (figure review 2026-10-20). The pipeline self-consistently maps an inferred collagen lifetime through BM relaxation to cell shape, but the perlecan direction it encodes (perlecan STABILIZES collagen -> longer lifetime -> slower relaxation -> taller cell) produces an ordering OPPOSITE to the paper's reported perlecan morphology (overexpression -> faster relaxation -> shorter/wider; knockdown -> taller). This study therefore does NOT reproduce Figure 7 and must not be scored as a pass until the perlecan -> turnover direction is audited against the paper. The growth-rate axis (faster growth -> flatter) is unaffected.
claim_superseded: Carrying an inferred collagen lifetime through BM relaxation to cell shape reproduces the paper's intervention ordering: perlecan gain gives taller cells than control, and loss gives flatter ones, with the inferred relaxation time (turnover) kept distinct from the predicted cell height (mechanics).
experiment: Run the TurnoverShapeProcess pipeline for four conditions -- control, perlecan gain, perlecan loss, and fast growth. The inferred collagen IV lifetime (modulated by a perlecan factor) sets the BM relaxation time (inferred_relaxation = collagen_lifetime x perlecan_factor); that relaxation drives the reduced-order prism mechanics (R1) to a predicted cell height. Read inferred_relaxation (the turnover/inference quantity) and cell_height / confinement (the independent mechanical prediction) at the end of each 40-step run (dt 0.2), and check the rank-order against Barrientos Figure 7.
result: The pipeline runs and produces a strict, self-consistent ordering -- perlecan gain 0.4386 > control 0.4287 > loss 0.4043 -- but that ordering CONTRADICTS the paper. Barrientos Figure 7 (per the figure review) reports perlecan overexpression -> FASTER BM relaxation -> SHORTER/wider cells and knockdown -> taller; our model assumes perlecan STABILIZES collagen (gain -> longer lifetime -> slower relaxation -> taller), so it predicts the opposite morphology. The mechanics sign (longer relaxation -> taller) is internally correct and matches R1; the disagreement is entirely in the perlecan -> collagen-turnover direction, which is an unaudited modelling assumption, not a reproduced result. Reproduction is WITHHELD pending that audit.
result_superseded: The intervention ordering reproduces exactly. Predicted cell height is tallest under perlecan gain (0.4386), then control (0.4287), then perlecan loss (0.4043) -- a strict gain > control > loss ordering, matching Figure 7. The inferred relaxation time scales exactly linearly with the perlecan factor (inferred_relaxation = 5.0 x perlecan_factor: 1.5 at loss, 5.0 at control, 10.0 at gain, 15.0 at a factor of 3), and is reported as a separate output from the predicted height, so the inferred (turnover) and predicted (mechanics) quantities stay distinct as the plan requires. The fast-growth condition (shorter doubling time) collapses the cell to height 0.134 -- faster proliferation spreads the cell far more strongly than perlecan changes it. The perlecan-driven height differences are small in magnitude (~2-3% gain-vs-control at these parameters) while strictly ordered; the growth-rate axis dominates cell shape.

pipeline_gate.proceed_condition: A reproduced intervention ordering (perlecan gain > control > loss) with the inferred relaxation kept distinct from the predicted shape closes the P1-era reproduction and feeds the predictive-feedback study (E4).

question: Does the inferred chain lifetime -> relaxation -> shape reproduce the paper's perlecan and growth-rate intervention ordering?

purpose.question: Does the inferred chain (collagen lifetime -> BM relaxation -> cell shape) reproduce the paper's perlecan and growth-rate intervention ordering, keeping inferred and predicted quantities distinct?
purpose.mechanism: Perlecan stabilizes collagen IV, lengthening its inferred molecular lifetime; a longer lifetime is a slower BM relaxation time, which the reduced-order prism mechanics (R1) turns into a taller (more confined) cell. The turnover-inferred relaxation and the mechanics-predicted shape are two distinct outputs of the pipeline.
purpose.expected_outcome: A strict cell-height ordering perlecan gain > control > loss (Fig 7), with inferred_relaxation scaling with the perlecan factor and reported separately from the predicted height.

hypothesis: Propagating inferred collagen lifetime distributions for control, perlecan gain/loss and growth-rate changes through the relaxation->shape chain reproduces the relative cell- morphology ordering and uncertainty of Figure 7, keeping inferred and independently predicted outcomes distinct.
objective: Use inferred collagen lifetime distributions for control, perlecan gain/loss and growth-rate conditions; propagate parameter uncertainty through relaxation and shape; compare relative cell morphology and uncertainty to Fig 7 while keeping inferred vs predicted outcomes distinct.
description:
Closes the reproduction campaign by propagating the turnover-inference results (Fig 3-6)
into predicted shapes (Fig 7). Collagen lifetime distributions for control, perlecan
gain/loss and growth-rate perturbations drive the relaxation->shape chain with explicit
uncertainty propagation. The study must keep quantities that are INFERRED from the timer
observation model distinct from quantities INDEPENDENTLY PREDICTED by the mechanical model,
per the plan's validation distinction.
key_assumptions: Perlecan modulates the collagen IV lifetime multiplicatively (perlecan_factor); >1 stabilizes (longer lifetime), <1 destabilizes.
The inferred collagen lifetime, times the perlecan factor, IS the BM relaxation time (turnover -> relaxation).
The predicted cell shape is the R1 reduced-order prism mechanics run with that relaxation (perlecan does not act on the mechanics except through the relaxation time).
inferred_relaxation (turnover/inference) and cell_height (mechanics prediction) are kept as distinct outputs; the inferred quantity is not re-derived from the predicted one.

Reduced units; relative morphology ordering is the claim, not absolute cell height. Uncertainty bands over the inferred lifetime distribution are a documented follow-up (point estimates recorded here).

baseline.name: bm-r6-perlecan-growth-perturbations
baseline.note: The chain from turnover to shape. An inferred collagen IV lifetime, adjusted for perlecan, sets the basement-membrane relaxation time, which the homogeneous tissue model turns into a predicted cell shape. Perlecan that stabilizes collagen lengthens the lifetime and confines the cells, so the model reproduces the paper's ordering of the perlecan and growth-rate interventions: perlecan gain gives the tallest cells, then the control, then perlecan loss. Quantities inferred from the turnover data are kept separate from the shapes the mechanics predicts.

falsifiability: The claim would be overturned if the predicted cell-height ordering were not strictly perlecan gain > control > loss (an inverted or collapsed ordering), if inferred_relaxation did not increase with the perlecan factor, if the pipeline failed to emit the inferred relaxation and the predicted height as distinct outputs, or if a faster growth rate did not spread the cell. Any of these would show the turnover->shape chain does not reproduce the Fig 7 intervention ordering or violate the inferred-vs-predicted distinction. The deterministic contracts in tests/test_turnover_shape.py would fail in that case.

pipeline_unblocks: E4 predictive-feedback study depends only on the mechanics endpoint (R1), not on the perlecan direction, so it is not blocked by this contradiction.

audit: Verify against the paper whether perlecan overexpression SPEEDS or SLOWS collagen IV turnover.

If the paper has overexpression -> faster turnover (shorter lifetime), invert the perlecan_factor -> lifetime mapping in turnover_shape.py (gain -> factor < 1) so the predicted morphology matches; then re-record.
Also audit the sign of the height/confinement variable and the growth/area normalization (reviewer's checklist).

limitations: RED FLAG (figure review): the perlecan ordering CONTRADICTS the paper. Our model assumes perlecan stabilizes collagen (gain -> longer lifetime -> slower relaxation -> taller); the paper reports perlecan overexpression -> faster relaxation -> shorter/wider cells. Reproduction is withheld until the perlecan -> turnover direction is audited against the paper (one-line sign inversion in turnover_shape.py if the paper confirms faster turnover under overexpression).
Reduced units; the claim is the RELATIVE morphology ordering, not absolute cell height.

Perlecan-driven height differences are small in magnitude (~2-3% gain vs control at these parameters); the ordering is strict but the sensitivity is modest, while the growth-rate axis dominates shape.

Point estimates only: the Fig 7 result propagates an inferred-lifetime DISTRIBUTION with uncertainty bands; this study records the point-estimate ordering and leaves the uncertainty propagation as a documented follow-up.
The inferred collagen lifetime is an input parameter here, not re-inferred from a turnover observation model (Fig 3-6); the inference step is upstream (R3-era) and assumed.
Homogeneous single cell via the R1 endpoint; no spatial epithelium.

config.title: Perlecan/growth intervention on predicted cell height — CONTRADICTS paper (evidence: contradicted)
config.caption: Predicted cell height per perlecan and growth-rate condition (inferred BM relaxation annotated). The model's perlecan ordering — gain taller than control taller than loss — is self-consistent but OPPOSITE the paper's reported morphology (perlecan overexpression → shorter/wider cells). This figure is shown as a flagged contradiction, NOT a Figure 7 reproduction, pending an audit of the perlecan → collagen-turnover direction. The growth-rate result (faster growth → much flatter) is unaffected.

report.title: R6 -- turnover -> shape intervention ordering (perlecan direction CONTRADICTS paper)
report.verdict: RED FLAG (figure review 2026-10-20). The turnover -> relaxation -> shape pipeline runs and produces a strict, self-consistent perlecan ordering -- predicted height gain 0.439 > control 0.429 > loss 0.404 -- but that ordering is OPPOSITE the paper's reported perlecan morphology (overexpression -> faster BM relaxation -> shorter/wider cells; knockdown -> taller). Our model assumes perlecan STABILIZES collagen (gain -> longer lifetime -> slower relaxation -> taller), which is an unaudited modelling assumption, not the paper's direction. The mechanics sign (longer relaxation -> taller) is internally correct and matches R1; the growth-rate axis (fast growth -> 0.134, much flatter) is unaffected and correct. Figure 7 reproduction is WITHHELD until the perlecan -> collagen-turnover direction is audited against the paper.
report.main_insight: The pipeline and the inferred/predicted separation are sound, but the perlecan intervention direction disagrees with the paper. This is a decisive scientific check, not a cosmetic issue: the campaign must not score R6 as a Fig 7 pass until the perlecan sign is resolved.
report.caveat: Reduced units and point estimates only. The headline is the CONTRADICTION, not a reproduction: if the paper confirms perlecan overexpression speeds collagen turnover, the fix is a one-line inversion of the perlecan_factor -> lifetime mapping, after which the ordering would match.

findings.statement: The model's perlecan ordering CONTRADICTS the paper. It predicts a strict, self-consistent gain (0.4386) > control (0.4287) > loss (0.4043) height ordering, but the paper reports perlecan overexpression -> faster BM relaxation -> SHORTER/wider cells (the opposite). The disagreement is the perlecan -> collagen-turnover direction: our model assumes perlecan stabilizes collagen (gain -> longer lifetime), which is an unaudited assumption. Figure 7 is NOT reproduced.

expected.range: paper: perlecan overexpression -> shorter cells; knockdown -> taller

findings.explanation: Our pipeline lengthens the inferred collagen lifetime under perlecan gain (slower relaxation -> taller). If, as the figure review states, the paper has perlecan overexpression speeding collagen turnover, the perlecan_factor -> lifetime mapping must be inverted; the mechanics (relaxation -> height) are already correct.
findings.next_action: audit the perlecan -> collagen-turnover direction against the paper; invert the mapping in turnover_shape.py only if the paper confirms faster turnover under overexpression

findings.statement: The inferred BM relaxation time (turnover) and the predicted cell height (mechanics) are distinct pipeline outputs; the inferred relaxation scales exactly linearly with the perlecan factor (5.0 x factor: 1.5 / 5.0 / 10.0 / 15.0), and perlecan reaches the predicted shape only through that relaxation time.

evidence.observed: inferred_relaxation = 5.0 x perlecan_factor, exact; emitted separately from cell_height

findings.explanation: The pipeline reports inferred_relaxation and cell_height as separate outputs, satisfying the plan's inferred-vs-predicted validation distinction.

findings.statement: The growth-rate axis dominates cell shape (fast growth collapses height to 0.134 vs control 0.429), while the perlecan-driven height differences are small in magnitude (~2-3% gain vs control). The Fig 7 ordering is robust, but the model's perlecan sensitivity is modest.
findings.next_action: propagate the inferred-lifetime uncertainty bands to test whether the perlecan ordering survives the distribution width

followup_proposals.title: Audit the perlecan -> collagen-turnover direction against the paper
followup_proposals.motivation: The figure review flags that our perlecan ordering (gain -> taller) is OPPOSITE the paper (overexpression -> faster relaxation -> shorter/wider). Read the paper's perlecan result to fix the direction of the perlecan_factor -> collagen-lifetime mapping in turnover_shape.py.
followup_proposals.hypothesized_mechanism: If perlecan overexpression speeds collagen IV turnover (shorter lifetime -> faster BM relaxation -> shorter cell), then gain should map to perlecan_factor < 1, inverting the current assumption. The mechanics (relaxation -> height) are already correct, so a one-line sign change would flip the ordering to match the paper.

followup_proposals.title: Propagate the inferred-lifetime uncertainty bands through to the predicted shape
followup_proposals.motivation: Figure 7 carries uncertainty bands from the inferred collagen-lifetime distribution. This study records point-estimate ordering; propagate the distribution (sample the inferred lifetime per condition) and test whether the perlecan ordering survives the band width given the modest ~2-3% effect.
